availability.note: bydautomotive.com.au/configurator/byd-atto-2-dmi 301-redirects to BYD's Build & Price flow; lists exactly two grades, Essential $24,990 and Premium $29,990, on 2026-11-27; CarExpert, Chasing Cars, RACV and EV Central launch coverage agree on two grades

listPrice.note: BYD configurator shows $24,990 (unlabelled; its drive-away is computed per state). CarExpert, Chasing Cars, RACV ('plus ORCs') and EV Central ('plus on-road costs') say before on-road costs in words for the same figure. A separate $25,990 drive-away campaign (configurator banner: NSW delivery, private registration; RACV: orders before 24 Dec 2026) sits below the app's Victorian round-trip of $26,998.38, i.e. a time-limited discount on on-roads, not a list price, so not used. carsales 'indicative drive away' $26,762-$28,193 brackets the app's $26,998

batteryKwh.note: CarExpert / Chasing Cars 7.85 kWh LFP Blade; BYD UK lists 7.8 kWh for the same pack. Nominal figure; no source states usable vs gross

rangeKm.note: BYD AU claim quoted by CarExpert/Chasing Cars/RACV as WLTP electric range 39 km on 16-inch wheels; BYD UK Active (same pack, 16-inch wheels) lists 24 miles WLTP, i.e. the same figure, so not an NEDC submission

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 7.85/39 x 100, matching byd-sealion-5's method. BYD's published WLTP EV-mode figure is 14.7 kWh/100km (CarExpert review, RACV) but is 25-27% below battery/range, which fails the build's cross-check against the nominal pack: the WLTP electric range appears to stop near BYD's ~25% charge-sustaining floor, so only ~75% of the nominal pack is used. The derived figure likely overstates EV-mode energy use by about a third

combinedRangeKm.note: WLTP electric 39 km + 45 L tank (BYD UK, CarExpert review, carsales) / 5.6 L/100km x 100 = 842.6, rounded

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: RACV: BYD's claimed 5.6 L/100km for both grades when the battery is low (charge-sustaining). BYD UK lists 55 mpg (~5.1 L/100km) WLTP combined for both trims; CarExpert recorded 5.5 L/100km on its short launch drive (battery state unstated)

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: combined label 1.8 L/100km (BYD claim with battery above 25%), at or below 3.5

isGreenForVicDuty.note: SRO: green passenger car = combined tailpipe CO2 <= 120 g/km; a 1.8 L/100km label is roughly 42 g/km (BYD UK Boost lists 41 g/km)

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: BYD AU page text: 425 litres, 1,335 litres with rear seats folded (its spec table repeats the BEV's 1,320 L and 345 km WLTP, a template error). Matched by BYD UK, CarExpert, RACV. Method unlabelled; UK spec lists a boot parcel shelf, consistent with to-the-cover

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: BYD AU page text 1,335 L folded, matched by BYD UK, RACV, CarExpert; method unlabelled

seats.note: carsales spec: 5 seats; BYD AU page does not state a count; 60:40 split rear bench per RACV

towKg.note: CarExpert review: 750 kg braked; carsales also 750 kg braked. BYD UK lists 750 kg under unbraked. No BYD AU technical sheet found

warrantyYears.note: BYD AU: 6 years/150,000 km vehicle; 8 years/160,000 km traction battery

insuranceAnnual.note: anchored between byd-atto1-essential ($23,990, $1,100) and byd-atto1-premium ($27,990, $1,200); $150 under byd-atto2-dynamic BEV ($31,990, $1,300) for its lower price

depreciationCurve.note: BYD brand curve [1,0.74,0.63,0.55,0.48,0.42] as on byd-atto2, byd-sealion-5 and byd-shark-6; one curve per brand (owner convention)
